scope: Primary inspection of the official monthly television schedule only; no radio mapping, runtime parser, media playback or rights certification.

source_record.title: ประจำเดือน ตุลาคม 2569

attachment.creator: Microsoft Excel 2021
attachment.source_url_policy: Resolve the current PDF from the stable public index in memory. Expiring download URLs and query credentials are deliberately omitted.

method.inspection: All four pages rendered with Poppler at 140 dpi and visually inspected; pdfplumber text extraction used only as a secondary check.
method.transient_url_handling: Selected the public index record in memory and followed its supplied PDF link; only safe metadata, stable index URL and content hashes are retained in repository evidence.

confirmed: The television index record is id 106, labelled October 2569, with numeric year 2026 and month 10 and update date 2 October 2026.
The PDF header independently identifies the parliamentary television station, October 2569 and an open-parliamentary-session schedule.
The content is a monthly recurring weekday template, not a dated daily listing. Month/year provide scope, but individual dates would have to be projected from weekday recurrence.
Page 1 contains the main linear TV grid, with separate weekday and weekend clock columns, merged cells, stacked programme titles, explicit duration labels and some repetition/accessibility markers.
Page 2 continues the legend/footer; page 3 contains production notes, including older show-start references; page 4 is blank.
Text extraction is possible; the main grid is not an image-only scan. Nevertheless, plain extracted text interleaves the two time axes and loses merged-cell associations.

timing_holds.observation: The large live Senate/House cells state that transmission starts at 09:00 and continues onward. A later grid boundary is not an explicit sitting end.
timing_holds.policy: Retain unknown ends; do not impose 16:30, 18:00 or a fixed sitting duration.

timing_holds.observation: The footer prints 00:00–06:59 for the closed-station page, while the same grid starts programmes at 06:00.
timing_holds.policy: Do not silently change the closure to 05:59 or move the morning programmes. Hold the conflicting interval pending clarification.

timing_holds.observation: The first programme column in the rendered header has no visible weekday name; subsequent columns identify Tuesday through Friday.
timing_holds.policy: Do not assign the missing label solely from column position; confirm the weekday mapping before recurrence expansion.

timing_holds.observation: Several source cells contain multiple short programmes, durations and shared time labels; not every title has its own unambiguous start and end.
timing_holds.policy: Export only intervals whose column, source clock and end/duration relationship are established. Do not turn every extracted title into a timed programme.

timing_holds.observation: The notes page includes older programme-start references, and index startdate is 2026-09-30 despite explicit October month/year metadata.
timing_holds.policy: Do not reinterpret recording/production notes as October air dates or expand recurrence from the unqualified startdate. Verify any future expansion within the explicit month and stated session context.

safe_timing_example_for_future_design.interpretation: This visually associated slot is a promising bounded case for a future coordinate-aware fixture. It is not exported or treated as an individually dated event in this pass.

next_step: Design a bounded current-index resolver that never persists presigned URLs, rejects stale or contradictory month/year records and detects a changed PDF layout.
Verify weekday column identity and merged-cell extraction against rendered samples from more than one month before adding a runtime PDF dependency or parser.
Project only validated recurrences to dates within the declared month, with documented recurrence provenance and Asia/Bangkok origin-time handling.
Keep live-ended blocks, ambiguous stacked titles, the unlabelled weekday and contradictory overnight closure outside XMLTV until resolved.
decision: Hold automated guide publication. The official current-month TV source is confirmed and useful, but its recurring layout and timing exceptions require deliberate parser design and additional validation.
